title: Microsoft is combatting tech support scams with partnerships, education and free in-store training
description: Each year 3.3 million people fall victim to tech support scams. Microsoft is fighting back with partnerships, education and free in-store training. Remember – never buy unsolicited software/services or give away control of your computer. Always take the caller’s information and report them: www.support.microsoft.com/reportascam

textual.observation: The description warns viewers against buying unsolicited software or services and against giving a caller control of their computer, then directs them to record the caller's information and report them.

evidence.quote: Remember – never buy unsolicited software/services or give away control of your computer.
Always take the caller’s information and report them: www.support.microsoft.com/reportascam

textual.context: Presented as warning and reporting guidance in an educational anti-tech-support-scam description, not as a promotion of the described conduct.
textual.potential_relevance: The source explicitly links unsolicited software or service purchases and requests for computer control to the stated tech-support-scam topic, providing a concrete mechanism and requested viewer responses for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish that any particular caller, website, transaction, identity or outcome is fraudulent, and the ASR does not provide relevant corroborating content.

visual.observation: A masked person tells a caller, “This is Sam from Microsoft. Your computer is at risk. For just $600 I’ll be able to clean the viruses.”
visual.context: The statement appears in a two-panel illustrated scene depicting a caller interaction.
visual.potential_relevance: The claimed Microsoft identity is linked to a request for $600 for computer-virus cleaning, which is a specific identity, payment, and service-claim relationship for review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame does not establish whether the interaction is real, whether any payment occurred, whether the speaker is actually affiliated with Microsoft, or whether the computer had viruses.

visual_context_notes.observation: The video visibly frames the topic as tech-scam protection and advises viewers never to buy unsolicited software or services, never give control of their computer, and report the caller.
The closing frames display Microsoft branding and a support URL containing “reportascam,” indicating a reporting-resource context.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents the $600 Microsoft-support claim as an illustrated example in anti-scam education, not as an offer from the publisher. It warns viewers about unsolicited software or services and surrendering computer control, and directs them to record and report suspicious callers. Microsoft branding and a reporting URL reinforce the awareness and reporting context, although the external site's behavior and any caller's identity or outcome are not established.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary theme is warning viewers about a depicted tech-support scam and providing prevention and reporting guidance, rather than soliciting payment, access, or participation.
